name: Ibrutinib
drug_class: Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor (covalent, first generation)
route_note: oral capsules, tablets or suspension once daily

discovery.by: Celera Genomics (Zhengying Pan and colleagues); Pharmacyclics acquired the programme in 2006
discovery.note: Designed as a covalent probe that binds cysteine 481 in the ATP site of BTK.

tagline: First-in-class BTK inhibitor that reshaped chronic lymphocytic leukaemia treatment
summary: Ibrutinib is an oral, irreversible inhibitor of Bruton tyrosine kinase, a key enzyme in B-cell receptor signalling. It was the first BTK inhibitor approved and changed the treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia, Waldenström macroglobulinaemia and chronic graft-versus-host disease, although atrial fibrillation and bleeding limit its use.
mechanism: Ibrutinib forms a covalent bond with cysteine 481 in the active site of BTK, permanently inactivating the enzyme and blocking B-cell receptor signalling to PLCγ2, NF-κB and other survival pathways.

Malignant B cells lose adhesion and homing signals and are released from lymph nodes into blood (transient lymphocytosis), where they undergo apoptosis. Off-target inhibition of kinases such as TEC, EGFR and CSK contributes to bleeding, rash and atrial fibrillation; the C481S mutation causes resistance.
uses: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (including 17p deletion)
Chronic graft-versus-host disease after failure of systemic therapy (adults and children)
Mantle cell lymphoma (outside the US; US accelerated indication withdrawn in 2023)

history.title: Pharmacyclics
history.detail: Pharmacyclics acquires Celera's BTK inhibitor programme.

history.title: B-cell signalling paper
history.detail: Honigberg et al. (PNAS) report PCI-32765 activity in models of B-cell malignancy.

history.title: Janssen partnership
history.detail: Janssen and Pharmacyclics agree to co-develop ibrutinib.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Accelerated approval for relapsed mantle cell lymphoma; among the first drugs with Breakthrough Therapy designation.

history.title: CLL
history.detail: Approvals for CLL after RESONATE, including 17p deletion.

history.title: AbbVie acquisition
history.detail: AbbVie acquires Pharmacyclics for about $21 billion; Waldenström approval.

history.title: Chronic GVHD
history.detail: First FDA-approved therapy for chronic graft-versus-host disease.

history.title: MCL/MZL withdrawal
history.detail: US accelerated approvals for mantle cell and marginal zone lymphoma are voluntarily withdrawn after confirmatory trial results.

pk.half_life: about 4–6 hours (pharmacodynamic effect lasts longer because of covalent binding)

facts: Its once-daily continuous dosing made CLL a condition many patients manage with tablets rather than chemotherapy.
